title: The /rankings Edge column and its buy/sell filter carry no signal for any of the 398 IDP rows, while /edge labels the same players BUY/SELL from a second, parallel detector
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md presents IDP as a first-class asset class on the blended board, and /edge advertises a market-gap BUY/SELL system. edge-helpers.js/marketAction is documented as 'Always rendered with an explicit state — never an ambiguous dash' (frontend/app/rankings/page.jsx:1164).
observed: _retail_source_keys() returns exactly {'ktcSfTep'}, and KTC publishes no IDP. _compute_market_gap therefore short-circuits to ('none', None) whenever retail_ranks is empty, which is every IDP row: the whole-board census is DL 145/145, LB 114/114, DB 139/139 = 398/398 marketGapDirection=='none'. In the browser (request-interception topology per AUDIT_PROTOCOL) all 43 IDP rows on /rankings page 1 render EDGE '—' while offense rows render BUY/SELL/HOLD. The advanced filter edge=buy|sell tests the same field, so it returns zero IDP rows by construction. Meanwhile /edge runs a SECOND detector, idpMarketAction(), anchored on idpTradeCalc, and renders 10 IDP SELL rows + 4 IDP BUY rows for players that /rankings shows as '—'. Abdul Carter (board #82), Micah Parsons (#80), Jared Verse (#84), Myles Garrett (#81), Caleb Downs (#145) are SELL on /edge and blank on /rankings; Nick Bolton (#112), Edgerrin Cooper (#102), Jordyn Brooks (#135), Fred Warner (#141) are BUY on /edge and blank on /rankings.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/data -o /tmp/w27.json && python3 -c "import json,collections;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));c=collections.Counter((r['position'],r.get('marketGapDirection')) for r in d['playersArray']);print({k:v for k,v in c.items() if k[0] in ('DL','LB','DB')})"
reproduction.expected: IDP rows carry retail_premium/consensus_premium like offense rows, or the UI states the exclusion per position
reproduction.actual: {('DL','none'):145, ('LB','none'):114, ('DB','none'):139} — 398/398. Browser DOM: 43/43 IDP rows show EDGE '—'.

numericProof.formula: marketGapDirection = 'none' iff retail_ranks == [] ; retail_ranks = [r for k,r in effectiveSourceRanks if k in {'ktcSfTep'}]

userImpact: A manager scanning /rankings for buy-low / sell-high candidates sees a blank Edge cell on every defender and concludes no IDP edge exists, in a league that starts 9 IDP of 21 slots. Filtering /rankings by 'Buy edge' silently drops 36% of the board. The same manager on /edge is told Micah Parsons is a SELL. Two pages, one concept, opposite answers, no reconciliation shown.

priorFinding.note: A05-F17 criticises the SCALE of the /edge IDP comparison (ladder-translated ranks averaged against an untranslated anchor). This finding is about a different half: that the /rankings Edge column and edge filter have no IDP path at all, and disagree with /edge about whether an IDP signal exists. Not a paraphrase — A05-F17 assumes the IDP detector is the only one; the contradiction between the two detectors is unrecorded.

whatWorks: /edge's IDP panels do compute and render an IDP buy/sell using idpTradeCalc as the anchor, and marketEdge()'s tooltip on /rankings honestly says 'No KTC rank for this player'. The refusal is honest at the field level; it is the two-surface contradiction that is not.
rootCause: 'Retail market' is defined as a single registry flag (is_retail) held by exactly one offense-only source. The gap detector was written for that one board and never generalised to a per-market anchor the way finder.py's gate was (src/trade/finder.py:538 IDP_MARKET_KEYS). /edge worked around it with a private duplicate instead of fixing the contract field.
requiredRepair: Make _compute_market_gap per-market — anchor IDP rows on idpTradeCalc the way src/trade/finder.py already anchors IDP assets — and stamp which market produced the direction (marketGapMarket). Then delete idpMarketAction/idpMarketEdge and let /edge read the contract stamp, so one definition serves both pages.
dependencies: Interacts with W27-F005: the same rank-space comparison is basis-blind for TE. Fixing the anchor without fixing the basis leaves the TE monoculture intact.

title: Trade suggestions cannot propose a defensive back to anyone — the top-150 board gate contains zero DBs — yet /trade tells all 12 teams to 'target DB' while every team already rosters 5-9 of them against a 3-DB requirement
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md and src/trade/suggestions.py:230-238 both assert the BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER gate ranks against 'our own blended board, which answers asset quality directly and for every asset class, including IDP and picks that no single retail board covers', and that sharing finder.py's gate 'would reintroduce the offense-only blind spot F-3 just removed'.
observed: build_asset_pool_from_contract(contract) returns exactly 150 assets: WR 41, QB 28, RB 26, PICK 23, TE 18, DL 7, LB 7, DB 0. The first DB in the full 812-row pool is Caleb Downs at board rank 167 (display_value 3159 against a board maximum of 9988). A single global top-N on a board where offense tops out at 9999 and the best defender sits near 6400 is exactly the failure mode finder.py:578-583 documents and fixes with a per-market cut — suggestions.py never got that fix. Consequence measured across all 12 rosters: 51 suggestion assets total, of which DL 5 and LB 11 and DB 0, and rosterAnalysis.needPositions contains 'DB' for 12 of 12 teams. Actual DB depth per team from sleeper.positions: Jason 8, Ed 5, Ty 7, Collin 7, MaKayla 7, Eric 8, Roy 6, Joey 8, Brent 9, Kich 7, jstuedle 5, Blaine 8 — against 3 mandatory DB starters. The engine reports a shortage at the one position no team has a shortage at, because starterCounts only counts pool members and no DB is ever in the pool.

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.trade.suggestions import build_asset_pool_from_contract as B;c=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));print(collections.Counter(a.position for a in B(c)));full=B(c,board_top_n=0);print([(i,a.name,a.display_value) for i,a in enumerate(full,1) if a.position=='DB'][:1])"
reproduction.expected: The pool contains DBs proportionate to a lineup that starts 3 of them (per-market cut, as finder.py does)
reproduction.actual: Counter({'WR':41,'QB':28,'RB':26,'PICK':23,'TE':18,'DL':7,'LB':7}) — DB absent; first DB at pool rank 167

userImpact: On /trade, the Trade Suggestions panel renders a red 'Should target DB' badge (trade-sections.jsx:1099-1103) to every manager in the league. Acting on it means spending real trade capital acquiring a defensive back at a position where the manager already has 167%-300% of the starters needed — and the engine can never actually offer one, so the advice is unfollowable as well as wrong. No warning is shown that the candidate pool has no DBs in it.

priorFinding.note: PRIOR-A14-F00/F01 describe the identical failure class in finder.py (offense-only pool) and are refuted at HEAD — see W27-F010. The twin defect in suggestions.py is unrecorded, and the code comment at suggestions.py:230-238 explicitly asserts the opposite.

whatWorks: DL and LB do reach the pool (7 each) and do appear in suggestions (16 of 51 assets across 12 teams). starter_needs_for_league correctly derives {DL:3, LB:3, DB:3} from the league's roster_positions. The failure is confined to the quality gate, not to IDP awareness in general.
rootCause: BOARD_TOP_N_FILTER is a single global cut over a value scale that is not comparable across asset classes: offense peaks at 9999, IDP at ~6400 and DB at 3159. finder.py identified this and ranks each market's own population from 1; suggestions.py kept the global cut and documented it as safe on the untested premise that 'our own blended board covers every asset class'.
requiredRepair: Apply the top-N cut per position family (or per asset class) in _apply_board_top_n_filter, mirroring finder.py's market_groups. Separately, rosterAnalysis.starterCounts must count the manager's WHOLE roster, not only pool members, or needPositions must be suppressed for any family with zero pool coverage and say so.
dependencies: Requires no data change; purely an engine-side gate change. Interacts with W27-F007 (hybrid eligibility) for how DL/LB counts are attributed.

title: The /angle page can never return an IDP player in a counter-package: the engine defaults include_idp=False and the page never sends the flag
claimUnderTest: server.py's /api/angle/packages docstring says 'Market value is per-position: IDPTradeCalc for IDP (DL/LB/DB), KTC for everyone else', and the /angle page's own hint reads 'KTC for offense, IDPTC for IDP' — presenting the page as IDP-aware.
observed: src/trade/angle.py:711 and :1216 both drop every IDP row from the candidate pool unless include_idp is true, justified in-code by 'most leaguemates don't gravitate toward them'. server.py:6526 defaults includeIdp to False. `grep -rn includeIdp frontend/` returns zero hits — frontend/app/angle/page.jsx:318-334 builds its body from mode/ownerId/playerNames/minMyGainPct/maxMarketGainPct/targetTeamOwnerIds/leagueKey only, and there is no UI control anywhere. Live A/B on the same request: includeIdp=false returns 10 candidates whose 18 assets are QB 10, WR 5, TE 2, RB 1 (zero IDP); includeIdp=true returns 13 candidates including 3 LB. The selected/offer side accepts IDP fine (an all-LB offer prices correctly on idpTradeCalc), so the exclusion is one-directional: you may give defenders, you may never be offered one.

reproduction.command: for v in false true; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/angle/packages -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"ownerId\":\"468418790212759552\",\"playerNames\":[\"Justin Jefferson\"],\"limit\":50,\"includeIdp\":$v}" | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);c=collections.Counter(p['position'] for x in d['candidates'] for p in x['players']);print(len(d['candidates']),dict(c))"; done
reproduction.expected: Both runs return IDP counter-assets in a 9-IDP-starter league, or the page exposes the toggle

numericProof.formula: idp_assets_returned_on_the_live_UI_path = 0 because include_idp = bool(body.get('includeIdp', False)) and the page never sets it

userImpact: A manager using the Package Builder to shop an offense piece is shown a return market that contains no defenders, in a league where 9 of 21 starting slots are defensive. Thirty percent of the plausible counter-packages (3 of 13 here) are withheld with no indication they were filtered, so the manager concludes no defensive return exists and either accepts a worse offense package or walks away from a fair trade.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding covers the include_idp default or its absence from the frontend body.

whatWorks: The offer side handles IDP correctly: an all-LB offer is priced on idpTradeCalc, carries market_uncertainty_band 1859 (16.8% of the total) and two explicit market_warnings naming the assumed offense<->IDP exchange rate. The exclusion is a candidate-pool filter, not a valuation failure.
rootCause: A deliberate default ('most leaguemates don't gravitate toward IDP') encoded as an engine-side hard filter rather than a user-visible preference, in a codebase where the only two live leagues on this scoring profile include one that starts 9 IDP. The parameter exists and works; nothing reachable sets it.
requiredRepair: Derive the default from the league's roster_positions (idpEnabled / IDP starter count) rather than a constant, and add an 'Include IDP' toggle to /angle that sends includeIdp. Cheapest correct fix: default include_idp to True whenever league_cfg's roster settings contain any DL/LB/DB/IDP_FLEX slot.
dependencies: None; the flag already threads server.py:6561/6603 into both angle entry points.

title: /api/angle/find applies a +/-5% cross-market plausibility gate that is narrower than the two boards' own measured p10-p90 disagreement, and stamps no uncertainty band
claimUnderTest: src/trade/angle.py:68-69 excuses find_angles from the cross-market machinery: 'find_angles (the 1-for-1 pivot) is untouched: it compares two single assets, so there is no cross-market sum to constrain.'
observed: There is no SUM, but there is still a cross-market SUBTRACTION, and the visibility gate is applied to it. Selecting an IDP player returns a candidate list that is 37 of 38 cross-market: the selected player's market_value comes from idpTradeCalc and the candidates' from ktcSfTep. With the default maxMarketGainPct=5 the endpoint returned exactly 2 candidates — Bo Nix at market_gain_pct 4.54 and Brock Purdy at 2.51 — both entirely premised on differencing an IDPTC number against a KTC number. Re-measured on this contract the paired IDPTC/KTC ratio spans p10 0.886 to p90 1.083 over 475 shared players, i.e. routine per-player disagreement of roughly +/-10%, twice the width of the gate. The response carries no uncertainty_band, no marketsUsed and no mixedMarket stamp — unlike /api/trade/finder (which stamps mixedMarket per trade) and /api/angle/packages (which returns market_uncertainty_band, market_gain_low_pct/high_pct and withheld_uncertain=311 on the same data).

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/angle/find -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ownerId":"468418790212759552","playerName":"Carson Schwesinger"}' | python3 -m json.tool | head -30
reproduction.expected: Cross-market candidates are either suppressed near the gate or stamped with the measured band, as /api/angle/packages does
reproduction.actual: 2 candidates at market_gain_pct 4.54 and 2.51, both cross-market, with no band, no marketsUsed and no warning

userImpact: Anyone calling this endpoint (no shipped page does today — /angle uses /api/angle/packages only) is handed IDP-for-offense pivots whose entire 'the market says this is fair' claim is smaller than the two boards' routine disagreement. The verdict is a coin flip presented as a decision.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced end-to-end on the live endpoint rather than by code reading: 37/38 candidates cross-market, 2 admitted at 4.54% and 2.51%, and the p10/p90 re-measured independently at 0.886/1.083 on today's contract. Priority lowered from the prior's framing because /api/angle/find has no UI caller — grep for '/api/angle/find' in frontend/ finds only the bridge route.

whatWorks: /api/angle/packages, which DOES go through src/league_intel/cross_market.value_package, gets this right: it prices single-market where it can, sizes a band from the same measured spread, withholds packages whose gap straddles the gate (311 withheld on a live run) and names the assumption in market_warnings.
rootCause: The cross_market rewiring covered the package path and explicitly exempted the 1-for-1 path on the grounds that only sums are dangerous. A difference of two numbers from different publishers carries the same scale risk as a sum of them.
requiredRepair: Route _make_candidate's market comparison through cross_market.compare_packages with single-asset packages, or at minimum stamp market_source per side plus a band and suppress candidates whose gain straddles the gate — the same posture /api/angle/packages already ships.
dependencies: src/league_intel/cross_market.py is already imported by angle.py, so no new dependency.

title: The market-gap direction is computed in RANK space where no TE-basis correction exists, so 33 of 33 edge-eligible tight ends are SELL and none is BUY
claimUnderTest: ADR-015 / CLAUDE.md: TE rows from non-TEP sources are lifted onto the board's tepp basis using KTC's own measured uplift, so the board is basis-consistent for tight ends.
observed: The basis conversion operates on VALUES inside the blend (data_contract.py:7674-7695). marketGapDirection is computed from ORDINAL RANKS (data_contract.py:3039-3056) and never sees it. ktcSfTep is the sole is_retail source and is a TE++ board; the consensus mean it is differenced against is dominated by base-TE boards. Measured on the live contract, mean(consensusRank) - mean(retailRank) by position: TE +41.60 (94.5% retail_premium), PICK +90.14, WR -6.83 (35.8%), RB -8.50 (25.8%), QB -24.69 (6.1%). Applying the /edge panel's own gate (canonicalConsensusRank <= 250, sourceRankSpread >= 20, not quarantined): TE 33 retail_premium / 0 consensus_premium, against QB 21 buy / 0 sell, RB 27 buy / 6 sell, WR 41 buy / 9 sell. Nine of the ten rows the Sell panel actually renders are tight ends (Eli Raridon, Mason Taylor, Greg Dulcich, Hunter Henry, Pat Freiermuth, Dalton Schultz, Max Klare, Travis Kelce, AJ Barner). On /rankings the same skew renders as TE 19 SELL / 0 BUY of the 23 tight ends on page 1.

reproduction.command: python3 -c "import json,collections;d=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));e=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if (r.get('canonicalConsensusRank') or 9**9)<=250 and (r.get('sourceRankSpread') or 0)>=20 and not r.get('quarantined')];c=collections.defaultdict(collections.Counter);[c[r['position']].__setitem__(r['marketGapDirection'],c[r['position']][r['marketGapDirection']]+1) for r in e];print({k:dict(v) for k,v in sorted(c.items())})"
reproduction.expected: TE buy/sell split resembles the other offense positions (roughly 1:3 sell:buy)

numericProof.formula: diff = mean(consensus ordinal ranks) - mean(retail ordinal ranks); diff > 0 => retail_premium => SELL. The tepp->base basis difference is a pure rank shift the value-space conversion never reaches.

userImpact: On /edge the 'Sell signals' rail is a tight-end list, and on /rankings 19 of 23 visible tight ends carry a red SELL badge. A manager who sells tight ends on that signal is trading away the position their two-mandatory-TE league is structurally short of, on the strength of a format artifact rather than a mispricing.

priorFinding.note: Reproduced independently. Counts differ slightly from the prior (33 of 33 edge-eligible here vs the prior's 36 of 36; top-250 offense census TE 35 sell / 0 buy vs the prior's 36 sell) because I gate on canonicalConsensusRank and the prior appears to have used a marginally different rank column — the direction and the 0-buy result are identical, and 9 of 10 rendered Sell rows are TEs in both.

whatWorks: The VALUE-space TE basis conversion is applied correctly and exactly once (see W27-F009), and the league-adjusted overlay's tePremium axis is deliberately ABSENT so it cannot double-count. The defect is confined to the rank-space gap label.
rootCause: Two different quantities share the name 'market gap': the value-space blend (basis-corrected) and the rank-space retail-vs-consensus mean (not). The correction was inserted at the value stage only, and nothing raised an error when the rank stage kept comparing a TE++ ordinal against base-TE ordinals.
requiredRepair: Either compute the gap in the basis-corrected value space (retail value vs blended value, both on the tepp basis), or rank-correct the retail side for TEs before differencing. A cheaper interim: suppress the direction for TE rows and say why, rather than emitting a signal that is 100% one-directional.
dependencies: Shares the anchor definition with W27-F001; a per-market anchor rewrite should fix both at once.

title: src/ros/ normalizes no position strings, so 6 IDP rows in /api/ros/player-values are bucketed as S/DT/DE and receive fabricated positional ranks like 'S1' and 'DE1'
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md: 'Position Normalization — Single source of truth: POSITION_ALIASES in src/utils/name_clean.py. All modules import from there.'
observed: No module under src/ros/ imports POSITION_ALIASES or normalize_position (grep returns zero hits across src/ros/*.py). The live /api/ros/player-values payload contains 500 rows whose positions include S 3, DT 2, DE 1 alongside the canonical DB 74 / DL 55 / LB 45. Because aggregate.py:275 buckets positional ranks on the raw string, Gregory Rousseau is stamped rosRankPosition 1 ('DE1'), Kamren Curl rosRankPosition 1 ('S1') at rosValue 15.96, and Christian Wilkins rosRankPosition 1 ('DT1') at 12.52 — each the notional #1 of a bucket of one to three players, while the real DB bucket holds 74 and the DL bucket 55. All six rows come from fantasyProsRosIdp.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/ros/player-values' | python3 -c "import json,sys,collections;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(collections.Counter(p['position'] for p in d['players']));print([(p['canonicalName'],p['position'],p['rosRankPosition'],p['rosValue']) for p in d['players'] if p['position'] in ('S','DT','DE')])"
reproduction.expected: Every IDP row carries DL/LB/DB per POSITION_ALIASES

userImpact: No shipped surface renders rosRankPosition today (frontend/lib/ros-index.js:119 indexes it and nothing reads it), so user impact is currently nil — but the payload publishes a positional rank of 1 for a replacement-level safety, and any future consumer that buckets by position drops these six players from their real family.

priorFinding.note: A18-F19 is about the CLIENT normalizePos omitting 7 IDP aliases. This is the server-side twin in src/ros/, which the prior does not name. Measured, not inferred.

whatWorks: src/ros/lineup.py compensates downstream with its own eligibility map (_SLOT_ELIGIBLE includes DE/DT/EDGE/S/CB), which is why /api/ros/team-strength still fills all 36 DL / 36 LB / 36 DB slots. Only the aggregate's own positional bucketing is affected.
rootCause: src/ros/ was written as a self-contained subsystem and never wired to the shared normalizer; lineup.py's private alias map hid the omission by making the visible surface work.
requiredRepair: Call normalize_position() in src/ros/aggregate.py where the display position is carried (:223-224) and where positional ranks are bucketed (:275). Then delete lineup.py's private alias sets in favour of the shared table.

title: DL/LB hybrid eligibility is implemented in exactly one subsystem (src/ros/); the /api/data contract carries no fantasyPositions, so 55 of 937 rostered players are single-eligible everywhere else and 32 of them disagree with Sleeper's own primary position
claimUnderTest: src/ros/lineup.py:84-89 states the correct rule — 'Sleeper evaluates eligibility against fantasy_positions, so a DL/LB hybrid legally fills either an LB or a DL slot. Checking only position (as this module used to) silently benches the player.' The question is whether anything outside src/ros/ obeys it.
observed: Intersecting the live Sleeper player file with contract.sleeper.idToPlayer: 55 of 937 rostered players carry more than one fantasy position — 50 DL/LB, 3 DB/LB, 1 DB/WR (Travis Hunter), 1 OL/OT. The /api/data contract exposes a single position per player: playersArray rows have a 'position' string and no 'fantasyPositions' key, and sleeper.positions is a flat name->string map. On 32 of the 55, the contract's position disagrees with Sleeper's own primary (Micah Parsons, T.J. Watt, Khalil Mack, Joey Bosa, Travon Walker and others are 'LB' to Sleeper and 'DL' on the board). grep for fantasy_positions/fantasyPositions across src/ finds it only in src/ros/{lineup,scrape,team_strength,playoff_sim}.py, src/league_intel/sim.py and src/public_league/snapshot.py — never in data_contract.py, suggestions.py, finder.py, angle.py or waiver.py. Consequences on the live payload: /api/trade/simulate returns starterDelta keyed {QB,RB,WR,TE,DL,LB,DB} from single positions; /api/trade/suggestions derives starterCounts and needPositions the same way (Jason's roster reports DL 1 / LB 3 while holding Andrew Van Ginkel, a DL/LB hybrid); /api/waiver/suggestions buckets by_position identically.

reproduction.command: curl -s https://api.sleeper.app/v1/players/nfl -o /tmp/sleeper.json && python3 -c "import json;sp=json.load(open('/tmp/sleeper.json'));d=json.load(open('/tmp/w27.json'));i2p=d['sleeper']['idToPlayer'];pm=d['sleeper']['positions'];h=[(n,sp[str(k)]['position'],sorted(set(sp[str(k)].get('fantasy_positions') or [])),pm.get(n)) for k,n in i2p.items() if str(k) in sp and len(set(sp[str(k)].get('fantasy_positions') or []))>1];print(len(h), sum(1 for x in h if x[1]!=x[3])); print(h[:5])"
reproduction.expected: The contract exposes each player's full eligibility so every engine can slot hybrids like src/ros/lineup.py does
reproduction.actual: 55 multi-eligible rostered players, 32 whose contract position differs from Sleeper's primary; 'fantasyPositions' absent from playersArray rows and from the sleeper block

userImpact: A manager holding four edge rushers that Sleeper lets him start at LB is told by /trade that he is thin at LB or DL depending on which label the board picked, and the trade simulator's starterDelta reports a positional swing that his actual lineup would not experience. The advice is wrong for roughly 6% of rostered assets, concentrated entirely in IDP.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding measures the hybrid population or notes that the contract omits fantasyPositions.

whatWorks: GET /api/ros/team-strength is genuinely first-class here and is the model to copy: on the live payload it fills all 36 DL, 36 LB and 36 DB slots across 12 teams with zero unfilledSlots, and 7 of those placements are cross-slotted hybrids (Nik Bonitto LB into a DL slot, Jeremy Chinn DB into an LB slot, Josh Hines-Allen DE into an LB slot, Andrew Van Ginkel LB into a DL slot). It reads Sleeper's fantasy_positions via src/ros/scrape.py:207-222.
rootCause: Eligibility was solved once inside the ROS lineup optimizer, where it was load-bearing, and the fix was never promoted into the shared contract. The contract's single 'position' string then became the de-facto eligibility model for every other engine.
requiredRepair: Stamp fantasyPositions onto playersArray rows (and into sleeper.positions or a parallel map) from the Sleeper player file the overlay already fetches, then have starter/need arithmetic in suggestions.py, trade_simulator and waiver.py resolve eligibility through it — reusing src/ros/lineup.py's _eligible_for_slot rather than adding a fourth alias table.
dependencies: Interacts with W27-F002: fixing the DB pool gate without fixing eligibility still mis-attributes 50 DL/LB hybrids.

title: CLAUDE.md's KTC-vs-IDPTradeCalc comparability claim reproduces on the live payload, ADR-025 is not in tension with it — but the summary hides a 10% TE-specific divergence that the code's own module docstring records
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md 'Cross-market note': 'of KTC's 500 rows, 475 also appear on the IDPTC board at a median value ratio of 1.000 (p10 0.888, p90 1.054, measured 2026-07-26). Both top out at 9999, so there is no rescaling to apply between them.' Set against ADR-025 in docs/consensus-edge/DECISIONS.md, 'idptradecalculator.com is the IDP market, and it cannot also be the IDP scale'.
observed: Re-measured independently on the live contract: ktcSfTep prices 501 rows, idpTradeCalc 911, and 475 are shared (94.8% of KTC). Pooled ratio idpTradeCalc/ktcSfTep: median 0.9970, p10 0.8864, p90 1.0826. Both boards max at 9999. The claim reproduces to three decimal places on n and p10. The two documents are NOT in tension: CLAUDE.md asserts unit comparability between two retail boards; ADR-025 asserts that a board cannot serve as the fair-value anchor its own market price is measured against (circularity), which is a different proposition about the consensus-edge board and does not deny comparability. What CLAUDE.md's pooled median hides is a single large positional divergence: TE median ratio 0.9000 (p10 0.8385, p90 0.9434, n=72) against QB 1.0322, WR 1.0103, RB 0.9939, PICK 1.0000. IDPTC's tight ends sit 10% below KTC's because KTC's is a TE++ board and IDPTC's is not — the same basis difference that drives W27-F005 — and the value-blend happens to neutralise it only because idpTradeCalc is registered is_tep_premium and so takes the flat 1.10 native correction (0.900 x 1.10 = 0.990).

reproduction.expected: 475 paired rows, median ~1.000, p10 ~0.888, both maxima 9999
reproduction.actual: 475 paired (94.8% of 501 KTC rows), median 0.9970, p10 0.8864, p90 1.0826, both maxima 9999; TE median 0.9000

numericProof.formula: ratio = idpTradeCalc / ktcSfTep per shared row; quantiles over n=475

userImpact: None directly — this is a documentation-accuracy finding. Its consequence is indirect: a reader who takes 'median 1.000' as licence to difference the two boards on a tight end is off by 10% before any real signal, and that is what W27-F004's gate does.

priorFinding.note: No prior finding re-measures the overlap. The TE divergence is already documented inside src/league_intel/cross_market.py:44-46 ('TE 0.895, the one real divergence'); it is CLAUDE.md's summary that omits it.

whatWorks: The core comparability claim is true and reproducible, and finder.py:264-280 already carries the p10-p90 caveat verbatim next to its mixedMarket stamp. idpTradeCalc's IDP maximum of 6444 against an offense maximum of 9999 confirms it is one shared scale, not a separately normalized IDP board.

title: The TE premium is applied exactly once per source per tight end — verified structurally on all 85 TE rows, with KTC exempt and the league-adjusted overlay's TE axis deliberately absent
claimUnderTest: ADR-015 / CLAUDE.md: TE rows from non-TEP sources are converted base->tepp with KTC's measured uplift; ktc/ktcSfTep are exempt; TEP-native sources keep a flat 1.10; and the double-count guard is structural.
observed: Audited every (TE row x source) stamp on the live contract: 85 TE rows, and no source on any row carried both tepBoostApplied and tepNativeCorrectionApplied. ktcSfTep is the only key with neither on all 73 rows it prices — the exemption. The eleven non-TEP sources take the measured curve (dlfSf min 1.2091 / median 1.3365 / max 1.4403; fantasyProsSf 1.2092-1.5915; flockFantasySfRookies up to 1.6367) — a genuinely rank-dependent uplift, never the flat 1.15 fallback. The four registry-flagged TEP-native sources (idpTradeCalc, dynastyNerdsSfTep, fantasyProsFitzmaurice, yahooBoone, draftSharks) take exactly 1.1000 on every row. The second insertion point where a double-count would live is closed too: /api/valuation/league-adjusted reports inactiveAxes ['tePremium', ...] and every TE row carries the single scarcity factor 1.011595, so the overlay contributes no TE-specific multiplier. The if/elif in data_contract.py:7674-7695 makes both branches mutually exclusive, and convert_te_value's two-basis API is a no-op when from == to, so a second call cannot compound.

reproduction.expected: 0 source-rows with both branches applied; ktcSfTep exempt; TEP-native sources exactly 1.10
reproduction.actual: 0 double-applied; ktcSfTep NONE on 73/73; idpTradeCalc/dynastyNerdsSfTep/fantasyProsFitzmaurice/yahooBoone/draftSharks native 1.1000 exactly; 11 non-TEP sources on the measured 1.209-1.637 curve

numericProof.formula: double_count = count(rows where tepBoostApplied AND tepNativeCorrectionApplied) + count(TE-specific multipliers applied by the league-adjusted overlay)

userImpact: None — this is a verified negative. The board's TE values are not inflated by a compounded premium.

priorFinding.note: A20-F04's claim that _BOARD_TE_BASIS is a constant that is wrong for dynasty_new is NOT tested here (only dynasty_main is loaded in this container, so the second league's basis is unverifiable). What IS tested and confirmed correct is the orthogonal claim A20-F04 relies on: the conversion happens once and the corrective overlay axis is ABSENT — verified live rather than by reading.

whatWorks: Everything in the exactly-once chain. Note the separate defect this does NOT protect against: the rank-space gap label ignores basis entirely (W27-F005).
requiredRepair: None. Preserve the mutually-exclusive if/elif and the two-basis (never a bare multiplier) API when refactoring.

title: The arbitrage finder's per-market IDP gate is live and working — the prior audit's claim that it is still offense-only does not reproduce at HEAD
claimUnderTest: PRIOR-A14-F00/F01: 'The trade finder receives no position data on the live path, so its per-market gate is inert and it is still offense-only', and 'the finder's explicit IDP-blindness warning cannot fire'.
observed: Does not reproduce. server.py:6188 now passes contract=contract into find_trades, and positions_from_contract() (finder.py:371) rebuilds the position map from playersArray, keyed on legacyRef/canonicalName/displayName. A live run against Jason vs all opponents returns metadata.marketCoverage {'ktcSfTep': 132, 'ktc': 18, 'idpTradeCalc': 150} — an IDP half that is exactly the per-market top-150 — and the 40 returned trades contain 120 assets of which 60 are IDP (DB 26, DL 23, LB 11). The league_has_idp detector at finder.py:1061 now reads the same repaired positions map, so it is reachable; it correctly stays silent here because idp_priced is 150, not 0. mixedMarketTrades is 0 on this run and every trade stamps marketsUsed + mixedMarket. title: The live board is blind to the league's IDP scoring: defensive backs are the cheapest family (best DB at board rank 167) even though this league pays 5.32 per pass defensed and 5.32 per interception against 1.33 per solo tackle
claimUnderTest: The workstream question 'does LB tackle volume automatically outrank scarcer DB/DL production?', and CLAUDE.md's framing of IDP as a first-class asset class whose format effects 'flow from exact scoring'.
observed: Measured on the live board, the answer to the tackle-volume question is NO in the direction expected and YES in a different one. Per family: DL n=145, max 6362 (Aidan Hutchinson, board pos 36), median 1376; LB n=114, max 5908 (board pos 44), median 1319; DB n=139, max 3159 (Caleb Downs, board pos 167), median 943. Edge rushers lead, linebackers follow, and defensive backs are compressed to roughly half the value at every quantile: the DL top-1-to-starter-depth ratio is 3.64x and LB 3.26x against DB 2.29x. That ordering is inherited wholesale from idpTradeCalc, a generic IDP calculator, and nothing in the live value path re-scores it under this league's actual settings — which pay idp_pass_def 5.32, idp_int 5.32, idp_tkl_loss 4.25, idp_ff 4.25, idp_sack 2.92, idp_qb_hit 2.13 and idp_tkl_solo 1.33. A 15-pass-defensed cornerback earns 79.8 points from that one category alone. The only league-aware IDP lever that reaches a value is the league-adjusted overlay's single per-family scarcity factor (DL 1.09776, LB 0.97971, DB 1.01183) — one constant per position, derived from roster structure, not from scoring; its tePremium and projectionCorroboration axes are ABSENT and there is no scoring axis at all. The subsystem that would close the gap, BDVM, answers status 'no_projection_snapshot' in this container.

reproduction.expected: IDP family ordering reflects the league's own scoring weights, or the payload discloses that it does not
reproduction.actual: DL max 6362 pos 36 / LB max 5908 pos 44 / DB max 3159 pos 167, with no scoring-derived adjustment anywhere and no disclosure

numericProof.formula: dbMax/dlMax = 3159/6362 = 0.497 — the best DB is worth half the best DL on a board that never reads a scoring setting

userImpact: Every DB decision on the site inherits a generic-format price. Concretely it is what puts zero DBs in the trade-suggestion pool (W27-F002) and what makes 'need DB' unfixable, and it means a manager in a pass-defensed-heavy league is systematically told his most format-advantaged position is his least valuable one, with nothing on the page saying the valuation is format-generic.

priorFinding.note: A24-F19 notes 12 canonical IDP scoring keys have no RULE_META entry so their contributions apply to every position bucket — a defect inside the scoring-fit machinery. This finding is upstream of that: no scoring-derived quantity reaches rankDerivedValue for IDP at all on the live path. Confidence is medium because 'the market is wrong about DBs for this league' is not directly falsifiable without a projection feed, whereas 'nothing in the live path reads the scoring settings for IDP value' is.

whatWorks: The IDP family ordering is internally coherent and on one scale with offense (idpTradeCalc's IDP maximum 6444 vs offense 9999 confirms a shared, non-renormalized scale). The lineup-structure half of league awareness is real: replacement.py measures starter thresholds from the exact optimizer over real rosters, and starter_needs_for_league reads roster_positions correctly.
rootCause: Market-rank ingestion is the only live value concept, and every registered IDP source publishes a format-generic board. The fundamental, scoring-exact concept exists (src/bdvm/) but has no projection snapshot in this environment, so the market board is the whole answer.
requiredRepair: Short term: disclose it — stamp on the contract (and note on /rankings) that IDP values are format-generic and not re-scored under the league's settings, the way ValueBasisNote already does for /draft. Medium term: land a projection feed so BDVM's exact-scoring path can supply the fundamental comparison the market board cannot.
dependencies: Blocked on data/bdvm/projections/ (a pre-declared Blocked-by-data condition) for the medium-term half; the disclosure half is unblocked.
